firsttoken oracle -- recorded from the REAL endpoint, host-side, 2026-08-30

THE ENDPOINT (chosen after evaluating five candidates; see the package report)
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    URL          https://api.llm7.io/v1/chat/completions
    method       POST (cross-origin from the guest page -> PREFLIGHTED: the
                 JSON content-type is not CORS-safelisted)
    request      Content-Type: application/json
                 {"model":"meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-Turbo",
                  "messages":[{"role":"user","content":
                      "Count from 1 to 8 slowly, comma separated"}],
                  "stream":true}
    response     200, content-type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8,
                 transfer-encoding: chunked (h1) / streamed DATA frames (h2),
                 access-control-allow-origin: *
    preflight    OPTIONS answers 200 with
                 access-control-allow-origin: *,
                 access-control-allow-methods: DELETE, GET, HEAD, OPTIONS,
                                               PATCH, POST, PUT,
                 access-control-allow-headers: content-type,
                 access-control-max-age: 600
    auth         NONE. No registration, no API key, no cookie. Anonymous
                 access is the service's documented free tier (probed live
                 2026-08-30 from this host).

THE RECORDING
-------------
oracle_headers.txt   the response head verbatim as our h1 client sees it
                     (captured with curl --http1.1, so the transfer-encoding
                     is the chunked one the ring-3 fetch actually parses).
oracle_body.sse      the DECODED body, verbatim: 26 SSE frames, 8595 bytes,
                     9 content tokens -> "1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8".
                     The offline gate (test-firsttoken-page) replays exactly
                     these bytes through a local cross-origin server that
                     answers the preflight and drips the frames -- the
                     parsing/rendering half of the proof, independent of the
                     endpoint's uptime. Nondeterminism is the reason this is a
                     RECORDING and not an expectation: an LLM's tokens are
                     never reproducible, but the bytes it emitted once are
                     stable forever, which is all a parser needs.

HOST TIMINGS (this capture; gateway cache HIT -- the uncached generation
below it is the honest "cold" number)
    ttfb   0.48 s     total 0.73 s    (cached: all 26 frames inside 0.25 s)
    ttfb   1.09 s     total 1.84 s    (uncached, measured earlier the same
                                       hour: same prompt, 26 chunks spread
                                       over 0.75 s of generation)
    Either way the first frame lands well inside the 30 s budget, and the
    frames arrive SPREAD OVER TIME, not as one burst: that spread is what
    makes this a streaming endpoint rather than a buffered one.

TO RE-CAPTURE (refresh the oracle against the current wire):
    curl --http1.1 -sS -N --max-time 60 \
      -A "Mozilla/5.0 (X11; LogitOS x86_64) Logit/1.0" \
      -H "Origin: http://10.0.2.2:18080" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{"model":"meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-Turbo","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Count from 1 to 8 slowly, comma separated"}],"stream":true}' \
      "https://api.llm7.io/v1/chat/completions" \
      -D oracle_headers.txt -o oracle_body.sse
